questions.question: Q1. When designing a dual-mode microstrip ring filter, what physical element is most commonly introduced to couple the two degenerate orthogonal modes and create a bandpass response?

answers.a: A continuous, perfectly symmetric grounding via in the center of the ring.
answers.b: A small patch perturbation, notch, or stub located at a 45-degree angle relative to the feed lines.
answers.c: An isolation resistor placed in series along the input transmission feed line.
answers.d: A secondary concentric outer ring with a completely different substrate thickness.

explanations.a: A symmetric grounding via does not provide the required mode perturbation for coupling the two degenerate orthogonal modes.
explanations.b: Correct. A small perturbation such as a patch, notch, or stub is introduced to disturb the symmetry of the ring and couple the two orthogonal degenerate modes, producing the desired dual-mode response.
explanations.c: An isolation resistor would introduce loss rather than provide the required mode coupling mechanism.
explanations.d: A secondary concentric ring can be used in other filter configurations, but it is not the conventional perturbation used to couple the two degenerate modes.

questions.question: Q2. In a conventional dual-mode ring resonator filter, the introduction of a perturbation element splits the single resonant frequency peak into two distinct resonant frequencies. What does this frequency splitting achieve?

answers.a: It transforms the filter behavior into a low-pass filter with infinite attenuation.
answers.b: It doubles the characteristic impedance (Z0) of the system without affecting performance.
answers.c: It produces a second-order bandpass filter response and can introduce transmission zeros for better selectivity.
answers.d: It cancels out all radiation losses, making the unloaded Q-factor approach infinity.

explanations.a: Frequency splitting does not transform the ring filter into a low-pass filter.
explanations.b: The perturbation does not simply double the characteristic impedance of the system.
explanations.c: Correct. Splitting the degenerate resonant mode into two nearby resonances provides the two poles required for a second-order bandpass response and can be used to improve filter selectivity.
explanations.d: Mode splitting does not eliminate radiation or other losses, and it cannot make the unloaded Q-factor infinite.

questions.question: Q3. For a microstrip ring resonator filter operating at its fundamental frequency, at what angular positions (relative to the input feed point at 0 degrees) do the voltage maxima (nodes) occur along the ring?

answers.d: Voltage is perfectly uniform at all angles across the ring perimeter.

explanations.a: The 45-degree and 135-degree positions are not the standard locations of the fundamental voltage maxima for the ring configuration described.
explanations.b: Correct. For the fundamental standing-wave distribution around the ring, the voltage maxima occur at positions separated by 180 degrees, corresponding to 90 degrees and 270 degrees relative to the specified feed point.
explanations.c: These positions do not correspond to the voltage maxima for the stated reference configuration.
explanations.d: The voltage distribution is not uniform around a resonant ring; standing waves produce distinct maxima and minima.

questions.question: Q4. What is a primary disadvantage of a basic microstrip ring resonator filter regarding its wideband performance?

answers.a: It can only handle low-power signals below 1 milliwatt.
answers.b: It completely lacks any resonant behavior if the temperature fluctuates by one degree.
answers.c: It suffers from periodic spurious passbands at integer multiples of the fundamental resonant frequency (2f0, 3f0, etc.).
answers.d: It cannot be measured using standard 50-ohm vector network analyzers.

explanations.a: A basic microstrip ring resonator is not inherently limited to signals below 1 milliwatt.
explanations.b: Temperature changes can shift the resonant frequency, but they do not eliminate the resonant behavior completely.
explanations.c: Correct. Ring resonators support higher-order modes, which can produce unwanted periodic spurious passbands at frequencies related to multiples of the fundamental resonance.
explanations.d: Microstrip ring filters can be characterized using standard 50-ohm vector network analyzers.

questions.question: Q5. To eliminate or suppress the unwanted harmonic responses (spurious passbands) in a microwave ring filter, which design technique is widely implemented?

answers.a: Replacing the copper microstrip line with high-resistance carbon filament.
answers.b: Using stepped-impedance resonators (SIR) or integrating defected ground structures (DGS).
answers.c: Removing the bottom ground plane entirely beneath the feeding structure.
answers.d: Decreasing the width of the ring until it reaches the manufacturing limit.

explanations.a: Replacing copper with a high-resistance material would increase losses and is not a standard technique for suppressing spurious responses.
explanations.b: Correct. Stepped-impedance resonators (SIR) and defected ground structures (DGS) are widely used techniques for controlling higher-order resonances and suppressing unwanted spurious passbands.
explanations.c: Removing the ground plane would disrupt normal microstrip operation rather than provide controlled harmonic suppression.
explanations.d: Reducing the ring width is not a reliable or standard method for eliminating higher-order spurious responses.
